column1: # Addresses established by reading the Linux disassembly, keyed by ELF build-id prefix.
# Read by tools/targets.py. status: at = the symbol is at `linux`; inlined = no function of its own in

# `witness` says what was seen, so that it can be seen again on the next build.

The two FixedString globals are used by one other function each, 0x4c19070, the EoCFS initialiser. Two callers, matching the oracle's two referrers: 0x2c2ac00 (the load flow -- reached from esv::SessionLoadSystem::Update 0x2c2b4b0, one level deeper than on macOS, and it goes on to esv::SavegameManager::LoadLevelCacheEntries 0x38a86b0) and 0x4198b00 (the save flow, which calls esv::SavegameManager::ThrowError 0x3b167a0). Registers as upstream declares them: rdi = OsirisVariableHelper* this, rsi = eoc::SavegameVisitor*, bool in al -- no LTO signature change.

ecs::EntityWorld::FlushECBs(), read instruction for instruction against the macOS oracle _ZN3ecs11EntityWorld9FlushECBsEv 0x1072e8f30 (targets.py left it unmatched: the whole ECS neighbourhood is -- EntityWorld::Update, Unload, ECBExecutor::Execute and EntityCommandBuffer::Flush all have no match). The prologues are the same instructions on the same members: `mov rX, [rdi+0x1f8]; test; movsxd rax, dword [rdi+0x204]; test eax,eax; lea rax, [rX + rax*2]` with rdi spilled between the two tests, both jumping to the same early-out, which sets [rdi+0x204] = 0. One argument, rdi = ecs::EntityWorld*; nothing sets al before the single `ret`, so the `bool` of upstream's signature is dead here. Its three Linux callers are macOS FlushECBs's four referrers modulo one level: 0x2d1e130 = ecs::EntityWorld::Update (the manifest row, hand-read) tail-jumps to it with rdi = its own `this`; 0x75b04b0 (calls ecs::EntityWorld::DeactivateSystemInternal 0x3659120, i.e. EntityWorld::Unload) calls it; and 0x3817fd0 tail-jumps to it the same way, itself called by ecl::EocClient::Load 0x4013620 (r1:15, a macOS referrer) and by 0x365d030 off ServerWorker::DoWork 0x2afbe70 (s1:0.84, the other). 0x3817fd0 is also upstream's own BinaryMappings.xml signature for this name read back: the bytes after its FlushECBs call are `mov rbx,[rsi+0x30]; mov eax,[rsi+0x3c]; imul rdi, rax, 0xf8`, and 0x3817fd0 is exactly that loop over [world+0x30] by 0xf8 with the count at [world+0x3c], on an object whose [+0x191] flag byte is the one EntityWorld::Update tests at entry. Two more readings say rdi is an ecs::EntityWorld in this build's measured layout: at 0x2487096 the spilled rdi (from [rsp+0x60]) is read at +0x300, +0x348 and +0x350 in one breath -- Executor, Cache and Settings.JobPriority, the three offsets EntitySystem.h's Linux asserts carry -- and they are handed to the inlined ECBExecutor::Execute(ImmediateWorldCache&, EWorkerThreadBatchPriority); and the caller 0x365d030 calls 0x3817fd0 with rdi = [EoCServer + 0x288], the server world's known offset. [world+0x300] is also the member upstream's Win32 signature tests for null before the call.

esv::functor::StatsFunctorDealDamage::Execute, the entity-target overload -- matched to the macOS oracle _ZN3esv7functor22StatsFunctorDealDamage7ExecuteERKN3eoc22StatsFunctorDealDamageERKN3ecs9EntityRefES9_RK8Vector3fbRKNS2_5spell9SpellInfoE... 0x1064cebc0 with only r3:2 / 1-of-3 evidence, so the argument list was read off the disassembly instead. The 18 slots of upstream's ApplyDamageProc land exactly where SysV puts them: rdi = the sret HitResult* (spilled to rbp; eoc::HitDesc::HitDesc(HitDesc const&) 0x27d7510 copy-constructs into +0, eoc::AttackDesc::AttackDesc 0x27d73d0 into +0x1a8, then +0x1c8..+0x208 are zeroed), rsi = the StatsFunctorDealDamage (spilled to [rsp+0xe0]), rdx and rcx the two ecs::EntityRef* (both read as {handle, world} with the 0x36/0x40 handle check and ecs::EntityRef::IsAlive 0x25c3960), r8 = Vector3f*, r9d = the bool. The twelve stack slots, with the frame at 6 pushes + 0xe18 = entry rsp + 0xe48: [rsp+0xe50] = spell::SpellInfo (passed as rcx, the SpellId const& parameter of eoc::spell::GetPreferredSpellCastingAbility 0x225f6b0), +0xe58 = storyActionId read as a *dword* (TypeWrap<unsigned int> by value, stored into the HitDesc copy at [rsp+0x810]), +0xe60 = ActionOriginator, +0xe68 = ClassDescriptions (passed as r8, GetPreferredSpellCastingAbility's fifth parameter -- the tell that nothing is shifted), +0xe70 = HitDesc and +0xe78 = AttackDesc (the two copy-ctor sources above), +0xe80 = the EntityHandle, +0xe88 = hitWith read as a *byte*, +0xe90 = conditionRollIndex as a dword, +0xe98 = the bool as a byte, +0xea0 = a17 dereferenced as a qword, +0xea8 = SpellId. Each of the four `push qword [rsp+...]` sites is 8 or 0x28 above its base offset because of a pending push. 14 callers here against the oracle's 14 direct E8 call sites. **The single `ret` at 0x3c4d054 does not set rax**, so the Itanium sret return value is garbage on Linux -- harmless, because upstream's wrapper returns whatever the original returned and the game's callers read the sret buffer.

esv::StatsSystem::ApplyDamage(ecs::EntityRefView<...> const&, eoc::HitDesc&, eoc::AttackDesc&, EAbility, bool) -- the macOS name for upstream's ThrowDamageEvent, which is why targets.tsv found no *ThrowDamageEvent* symbol. Both this and the oracle 0x106530750 are unmatched, so the identity rests on four readings. (1) The call site inside stats__DealDamageFunctor__ApplyDamage: at 0x3c4c72a rdi is the object at [[EntityWorld+0x30] + TypeId<esv::StatsSystem, ecs::SystemsContext>::m_TypeIndex 0x7cef3e8 * 0xf8] -- the StatsSystem singleton out of the world's SystemTypeEntry array, read at 0x3c4b41e and kept at [rsp+0xb0] -- with rsi = an EntityRefView local, rdx = the HitDesc at [rsp+0x7c8], rcx = the AttackDesc inside the HitResult, r8d and r9d the two flags; and the instruction after the call is `cmp byte [rsp+0x7ce], 0xa`, which is upstream's own BinaryMappings.xml signature for this name read back (`cmp byte ptr [rbp+var_B10+6], 0Ah`, var_B10 being the HitDesc it passes in r8 on Win64). (2) Prologues, instruction for instruction: macOS spills rdx and rdi, loads [rsi], does `shr 0x36 / cmp 0x40 / ja BAIL`, takes [rsi+8] and tests it, spills r8d and r9d, then `cmp qword [rsi+0x50], 0 / je L / movaps xmm0, [rsi+0x50] / eax = dword [rsi+0x60]`; Linux 0x330fe20 does the same in the same order on the same members (+8, +0x50, +0x60), rsp-relative and without the stack-protector load. (3) The class's own method takes rdi as `this`: at 0x330ff4e the entry rdi (via [rsp+0x28]) is rdi again for esv::StatsSystem::SetCurrentHitPoints(ecs::WorldView<...>&, EntityRefView<HealthComponent> const&, int) 0x2eeffc0, with rsi = [rdi+8], the system's EntityWorld. (4) What the body does is damage: TypeId<eoc::stats::EntityDamagedEventOneFrameComponent, ComponentTypeIdContext>::m_TypeIndex 0x7ce4830 (upstream's neighbouring ThrowEntityDamagedEvent name), TypeId<eoc::HealthComponent, sync::ReplicatedTypeContext> 0x7d06e70, GetComponentsForView<HealthComponent> 0x70ecb50 and the ECB's EnsureNode 0x21ddf50. 4 callers here against the oracle's 4 direct E8 call sites, one of them ApplyDamage on both sides.
